title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a schematic overview of the 'Teichmüller tower' organized by genus. The notation Γ^{!+}_{g,ν} denotes the pure ('!', numbered marked points), orientation-preserving ('+') mapping class group of a genus-g surface with ν marked points. The symmetric groups 𝔖_ν written above the genus-0 row are the groups acting on the numbered points.

(1) Genus 0. There is a tower Γ_{0,ν} → Γ_{0,ν-1} → … → Γ_{0,4} → Γ_{0,3} = {1}, given by forgetting the last point. Each step has kernel Π_{0,ν-1}, the fundamental group of the sphere minus ν-1 points (Birman exact sequence). Inside each Π sits a subgroup L_0^{(0,ν-1)}. This is most plausibly the intersection of a canonical commutative subgroup of Γ_{0,ν} with the point-pushing kernel: it has rank ≥ 1 because the rank drops by one along the forgetful map. Margin note: in Γ_{0,ν} (ν ≥ 4) there are canonical commutative subgroups ('nilpotent' crossed out) of rank ν-3, i.e. ≅ ℤ^{ν-3}. These are the free abelian groups generated by Dehn twists along a pants decomposition. Equivalently, they are the (pro-finitely: inertia) groups at maximally degenerate stable curves, i.e. the 0-dimensional boundary strata of M̄_{0,ν}.

(2) Pictures. Points 0, 1, 2, 3, …, ν-1, ν on a line, and a circle around 0 with the points 1 and ∞. Together with the inclusion k[x_1,…,x_ν] ⊂ k{x_1}{x_2}…{x_ν} (iterated Laurent/power series), these describe a 'tangential base point' at a maximally degenerate point. An ordered configuration in which x_1 is infinitesimal relative to x_2, x_2 relative to x_3, and so on gives a fiber functor via an embedding of the function field into an iterated Laurent series field. The inertia of that point is the abelian group above.

(3) Genus 1. Tower Γ_{1,ν} → … → Γ_{1,1} ≅ SL(2,ℤ), with kernels Π_{1,ν-1}, …, Π_{1,1}. Inside SL(2,ℤ) the subgroup L_0^Θ is presumably the unipotent (Dehn-twist / cusp) ℤ. Canonical commutative subgroups have rank ν (= 3·1 - 3 + ν).

(4) Genus g ≥ 2, ν ≥ 0. Tower down to Γ_{g,0}, with kernels Π_{g,ν-1}, …, Π_{g,1}, Π_g. Inside Π_g sits Λ_g ≅ ℤ, followed by a '?': in a closed surface group, commutative subgroups are cyclic. Inside Γ_{g,0} is a subgroup Δ_g ≅ ℤ^g, probably twists along g disjoint non-separating curves. The stated rank of the canonical commutative subgroups was first written 2g (crossed out), then 3g+ν.

Purpose: to set up base points 'at infinity' (maximal degenerations / pants decompositions) and their inertia groups for the fundamental groupoids of the Teichmüller tower. This is the program of the Esquisse d'un programme (Galois action on the tower, 'Lego' assembled from M_{0,4} and M_{1,1}).
errors: Γ^{!+}_{0,4} ≅ SL(2,ℤ)/±1 is wrong for the pure group, which is what '!' must mean here since Γ^{!+}_{0,3} = {1}. The pure mapping class group of the 4-punctured sphere is free of rank 2 (≅ Γ(2)/±1, index 6 in PSL(2,ℤ)). The diagram itself shows this: the kernel Π_{0,3} = F_2 of Γ_{0,4} → Γ_{0,3} = 1 must be all of Γ_{0,4}. PSL(2,ℤ) is related to the non-pure group or the quotient by the Klein four group.

The rank 3g+ν for g ≥ 2 should be 3g-3+ν. This is the maximal rank of abelian subgroups of the mapping class group: twists along a pants decomposition. It is also the rank consistent with the page's own values ν-3 for g=0 and ν for g=1.
Δ_g ≅ ℤ^g under Γ_{g,0} is not the canonical (maximal) commutative subgroup, which has rank 3g-3. It is at best a partial multitwist group; its role is unclear.
Λ_g ≅ ℤ ⊂ Π_g is marked '?'. Its definition is not made precise on the page.

ideas.what: Tower of pure mapping class groups linked by forgetful maps, with kernels the surface groups Π_{g,ν-1}
Canonical free abelian subgroups of rank 3g-3+ν attached to maximal degenerations / pants decompositions
ideas.modern_name: Multitwist groups / inertia at maximally degenerate stable curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birman–Lubotzky–McCarthy (1983) for maximal rank; Ihara–Nakamura (1997) arithmetic version
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (pants decompositions as base points 'at infinity'), stated informally

ideas.what: Base point at a maximally degenerate point given by embedding k[x_1..x_ν] into iterated Laurent series k{x_1}…{x_ν}, with ordered configuration 0,1,…,ν
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points at maximal degeneration (Deligne-type tangential base points; Ihara–Nakamura deformation)
ideas.where_published: Spirit in Esquisse; the explicit iterated-series formulation is not, to my knowledge, in his published texts

missed.claim: An early explicit sketch (1981–83) of base points at maximally degenerate curves defined by embedding the coordinate ring into iterated Laurent series. This predates the Ihara–Nakamura formalization and is of historical-priority interest only.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents that Grothendieck had the iterated-series model of tangential base points for M_{0,n} and M_{g,n}, later standard in Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a summary sketch of standard structure (Birman sequences, multitwist subgroups of rank 3g-3+ν) that Grothendieck himself publicized in the Esquisse and that was later formalized by Ihara–Nakamura. Only the iterated Laurent-series base point is a mildly notable detail. The page also contains slips (Γ_{0,4}, rank 3g+ν).
transcription_corrections: The groups are written Γ (drawn like τ); top-left label is Γ^{!+}_{g,ν} (the '!+1' in the genus ≥2 row is just '!+').
Γ^{!+}_{0,3} = {1}; a scribbled crossed-out attempt precedes {1}.
Margin, genus 0: 'dans Γ^{!+}_{0,ν} (ν≥4) ss-groupes canoniques ~~nilpotents~~ commutatifs de rang ν-3 (i.e. ≅ ℤ^{ν-3})'.
Genus ≥2 margin: rank first written '2g' (crossed out), then '3g+ν'.
Under Γ_{0,ν} the kernel is Π_{0,ν-1}, and the bottom-left label is L_0^{(0,ν-1)}.
Crossed-out bottom formula ends with '≤ (ν-2)(ν-3)/2'; the rest is illegible.
